=== coral --help-all
exit 0
--- stdout
Coral: AI agents on this computer, in one dashboard.

Usage:
  coral [flags]              start the Coral server (the dashboard)
  coral <command> [flags]    run one command against this computer's Coral

Commands:
  open             sign in to the dashboard: opens it in your browser (--print: just print the one-time link)
  api-key          print this Coral's API key (a script sends it as: Authorization: Bearer <key>)
  set-password     set the dashboard's first password, on a running Coral
  reset-password   set a new password, or none (--clear); every browser is signed out
  setup-code       print the one-time code that setting the password from another computer asks for
  cloud            Coral Hub: connect this Coral, show its status, or disconnect
  machine          make a cloud machine that runs Coral and joins Coral Hub (a pending machine you approve there)
  auto-accept      turn auto-accept off for every agent at once
  artifacts        prune stored artifacts (diffs and objects) to free disk
  db               compact the database, or rebuild its search index (stop Coral first)
  version          print the version (also --version, -v)
  help             this help, or a command's: coral help <command>

Main server flags:
  --port N         port to listen on (default DEFAULTPORT)
  --host ADDR      address to listen on (default: this computer only)
  --home DIR       data folder (default: CORAL_DATA_DIR, else .coral in your home folder)
  --no-browser     don't open the dashboard in the browser at startup
  --cloud-url URL  the Coral Hub this server may connect to ("off" disables it)

Run 'coral help <command>' for a command's flags, and 'coral --help-all' for every server flag.

Every server flag:
  -agent-priority string
    	Priority of agent processes: low (default, nice +10 / below normal so the server stays responsive) or normal. Also CORAL_AGENT_PRIORITY or the Settings choice
  -allow-shared-data-dir
    	Run even when the data folder can be read by other accounts and Coral can't make it private (Windows: it is owned by someone else, or is a link). By default Coral makes such a folder private to you, or refuses to start (also CORAL_ALLOW_SHARED_DATA_DIR=1)
  -backend string
    	Terminal backend: pty or tmux (default: Settings > Terminal backend, else pty: agents stop when you quit Coral)
  -bootstrap-file string
    	One-time Coral Hub credential file to enroll this server with at startup (owned by you, mode 0600, removed after reading). On Linux /run/coral/bootstrap.d/credential is read without the flag
  -cloud-connect string
    	Offer to connect to Coral Hub on a server not yet connected (also CORAL_CLOUD_CONNECT): prompt (the dashboard's first-launch screen, and a prompt in the terminal at startup; without a terminal, log the link and code), auto (the screen, and only log them) or off. Unset: prompt when --cloud-url/CORAL_CLOUD_URL is given, otherwise off (the build's default URL alone offers nothing; Coral Hub stays in Settings, on the home screen and in 'coral cloud connect')
  -cloud-max-mode string
    	Most Coral Hub may do on this computer: view, interact or launch (also CORAL_CLOUD_MAX_MODE). Sets the same cap as Settings > Coral Hub, at startup, for a machine nobody sits at (a container); an invalid value stops Coral from starting. Unset leaves the saved setting (view by default). Only whoever starts Coral can set it: the hub and the API cannot
  -cloud-url string
    	Coral Hub origin this server may connect to (also CORAL_CLOUD_URL). Release builds default to https://app.coralhub.dev; "" or off disables it. Nothing is sent until you connect
  -debug-input
    	Record every write Coral makes to agent terminals in <data dir>/input-debug.log (debug; may contain secrets). Also CORAL_DEBUG_INPUT=1 or the Settings toggle
  -encryption-self-test
    	Run an isolated encrypted database round-trip and exit
  -home string
    	Data directory (default: ~/.coral)
  -host string
    	Address to listen on, or a comma list of them (e.g. 127.0.0.1,100.101.102.103). Default: this computer only. A network address (or 0.0.0.0) is used only when remote access is on (Settings > Privacy, or --remote); otherwise Coral listens on 127.0.0.1
  -hub
    	Run as a multi-server hub: manage and view remote Coral servers (also CORAL_HUB=1)
  -no-auto-loopback
    	When --host names only network addresses, don't also listen on 127.0.0.1 (also CORAL_NO_AUTO_LOOPBACK=1)
  -no-browser
    	Don't open the browser on startup
  -port int
    	Port to bind to
  -proof-file string
    	Optional proof file to send with the bootstrap credential (at most 16 KiB of JSON from a provider helper)
  -remote
    	Allow remote (non-loopback) connections without requiring the saved setting
  -strict-local-auth
    	Require a credential for every request from this computer: an agent's session token, the dashboard's sign-in (run 'coral open' to sign in), a command-line signature or the API key ('coral api-key'); refuse an agent acting as someone else. On by default; --strict-local-auth=false turns it off (CORAL_STRICT_LOCAL_AUTH=0 does too, in a dev build only), which lets any program on this computer use Coral without a credential (default true)
  -tls-cert string
    	PEM certificate file: serve HTTPS (and WSS) on the port, and accept only HTTPS from other computers. Needs --tls-key (also CORAL_TLS_CERT)
  -tls-key string
    	PEM private key file for --tls-cert (also CORAL_TLS_KEY)
  -v	Print the version and exit
  -version
    	Print the version and exit (also -v, or coral version)
--- stderr
=== coral --no-browser --port abc
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
coral: invalid value "abc" for flag -port: parse error
Run 'coral --help' for the commands and main flags, or 'coral --help-all' for every server flag.
=== coral --no-browser --port
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
coral: flag needs an argument: -port
Run 'coral --help' for the commands and main flags, or 'coral --help-all' for every server flag.
=== coral --no-browser --cloud-max-mode bogus
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
--cloud-max-mode / CORAL_CLOUD_MAX_MODE must be view, interact or launch, got "bogus"
=== coral --no-browser --cloud-connect bogus
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
--cloud-connect (or CORAL_CLOUD_CONNECT) must be prompt, auto or off (got "bogus")
=== coral --no-browser --agent-priority bogus --encryption-self-test
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
database encryption is not included in this standard build; experimental encryption requires a build with CGO_ENABLED=1 and -tags sqlcipher,fts5
=== coral --no-browser stop
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
coral: unexpected argument "stop"
Coral runs until you stop it: Ctrl+C in its window, or Quit in the Coral tray (coral-tray --stop stops the tray).
Run 'coral --help' for the commands and main flags, or 'coral --help-all' for every server flag.
=== coral --no-browser --no-such-flag
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
coral: unknown option "--no-such-flag"
Run 'coral --help' for the commands and main flags, or 'coral --help-all' for every server flag.
=== coral -h
exit 0
--- stdout
Coral: AI agents on this computer, in one dashboard.

Usage:
  coral [flags]              start the Coral server (the dashboard)

  db               compact the database, or rebuild its search index (stop Coral first)

Run 'coral help <command>' for a command's flags, and 'coral --help-all' for every server flag.
